questions.question: A can run 1 km in 4 min, and B can cover the same distance in 4 min 10 sec. By what distance can A beat B in a 1 km race?
questions.solution:
**Given Data:**

A runs 1 km in 4 min.

B runs 1 km in 4 min 10 sec.

**Concept:**

Distance = Speed × Time

**Solution:**

4 min = 240 sec. & 4 min 10 sec = 250 sec.

A covers 1 km in 240 sec, B covers 1 km in 250 sec, 

Speed of B ⇒ 1km/250sec = 1000meter/250sec = 4 m/sec. 

Difference of Time between A & B = 250 - 240 = 10 sec.

A can beat B 10 sec prior,

Distance = 4 × 10 = 40 m.

**∴ A beat B by 40 m.**

questions.question: A sum of money doubles itself at compound interest in 10 years. In how many years will it be four times at the same rate of interest?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In Compound Interest, if a sum becomes 'n' times in 'T' years, it becomes 'nk' times in 'k × T' years.

Here, the sum doubles (2 times) in 10 years (n = 2, T = 10).

To become four times (4 = 2²), the power k = 2.

Time required = k × T = 2 × 10 = 20 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 20 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial Sum = P

Amount after 10 years = 2P

Target Amount = 4P

**Formula Used:**

A = P(1 + r/100)t

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e36ae2a959de069380b62e30ec5538143e6b211b4a1e20a7f6b60d6ddc39ece2.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 2P = P(1 + r/100)¹⁰

⇒ 2 = (1 + r/100)¹⁰ ---- (i)

⇒ Let the required time be 't' years for the sum to become 4P.

⇒ 4P = P(1 + r/100)t

⇒ 4 = (1 + r/100)t

⇒ (2)² = (1 + r/100)t

⇒ Substituting value of 2 from (i):

⇒ [(1 + r/100)¹⁰]² = (1 + r/100)t

⇒ (1 + r/100)²⁰ = (1 + r/100)t

⇒ By comparing powers, t = 20 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 20 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Effective Rate of Interest

When interest is compounded more than once a year, the effective annual rate is (1 + r/n)ⁿ − 1, where n is the frequency of compounding.

Rule of 72

A quick way to estimate how long it takes to double money at CI: Time ≈ 72 ÷ Interest Rate.

SI vs CI for Doubling

In Simple Interest, if a sum doubles in T years, it becomes n times in (n−1) × T years. For 4 times, it would take (4−1) × 10 = 30 years.</p

questions.question: If 90 is divided into two parts in the ratio of 2 ∶ 3, then what are the values of two parts?
questions.solution:
**Given Data:**

90 is divided into two parts in the ratio of 2 ∶ 3.

**Solution:**

⇒ The two parts are 2x and 3x (where x is the common ratio).

According to the problem,

⇒ 2x + 3x = 90

⇒ 5x = 90.

⇒ x = (90)/(5) = 18.

the two parts are 2x = 36 and 3x = 54.

**Therefore, the values of two parts are 36 and 54.**

questions.question: The weight of five boys is recorded as 22.450 kg, 24.150 kg, 24.720 kg, 28.530 kg and 25.150 kg. What is the average weight of all the five boys?
questions.solution:
**Concept:**

Average = Sum of observations/Number of observations.

**Solution:**

Sum of weights = 22.450 kg + 24.150 kg + 24.720 kg + 28.530 kg + 25.150 kg = 125 kg.

⇒ Average weight = (125)/(5) = 25 kg.

**Therefore, the average weight of all the five boys is 25 kg.**

questions.question: A bus covered a distance of 72 km in 60 min. What is the speed of the bus in km/h?
questions.solution:
**Given Data:**

Distance = 72 km.

Time = 60 min.

**Concept:**

Speed = Distance/Time.

**Solution:**

⇒ Speed = (72)/(1) = 72 km/h.

**Therefore, the speed of the bus is 72 km/h.**

questions.question: A lady professes to sell sugar at 20% profit on the cost price and using a weight which is 30% less than the actual measure. What is her gain percentage?
questions.solution:
**Given Data:**

Lady sells sugar at 20% profit and,

Uses a weight 30% less than the actual measure.

**Formula Used:**

Actual Profit% = [(P + W) / (1 - W)] × 100

Profit% = P (in decimal)

Less weight% = W (in decimal)

**Solution:**

20% = 0.2 & 30% = 0.3

Actual Profit% = [(P + W) / (1 - W)] × 100

⇒ Actual Profit% = [(0.2 + 0.3)/(1 - 0.3)] × 100

⇒ Actual Profit% = (0.5/0.7) × 100

⇒ Actual Profit% = 500/7

⇒ Total gain% = 71(3)/(7)\%

**Therefore, her gain percentage is 71(3)/(7)\%.**

questions.question: A and B together can do a piece of work in 20 days, and B and C together can do the same work in 100 days. If B alone can do the same work in 140 days, then in how many days will A and C together can complete the same work?
questions.solution:
**Given Data:**

A and B can do a piece of work in 20 days.

B and C can do the same work in 100 days.

B alone can do the same work in 140 days.

**Concept:**

Work done = Efficiency × Number of Days

**Solution:**

⇒ Work done by (A + B) in a day = 1/20.

⇒ Work done by (B + C) in a day = 1/100.

⇒ Work done by B in a day = 1/140.

⇒ Work done by A in a day = (A + B) - B = 1/20 - 1/140 = 6/140 = 3/70.

⇒ Work done by C in a day = (B + C) - B = 1/100 - 1/140 = 2/700 = 1/350.

⇒ Therefore, A and C together can do the work in 1/(A + C) = 1/(3/70 + 1/350) = 1/(4/70) = 175/8 days.

**Therefore, A and C together can complete the same work in 175/8 days.**

questions.question: A can do a piece of work in 4 days, while B can do it in 8 days. If they work on alternate days beginning with A, then in how many days will the work be completed?
questions.solution:
**Given Data:**

A can do a piece of work in 4 days.

B can do it in 8 days.

**Concept:**

Work done by A and B in one cycle of two days when they work on alternate days.

**Solution:**

⇒ Work done by A in a day = 1/4.

⇒ Work done by B in a day = 1/8.

⇒ Work done by A and B in 2 days = 1/4 + 1/8 = 3/8.

⇒ Therefore, in 4 days they will complete 2*3/8 = 6/8 = 3/4 of the work.

⇒ Remaining 1/4 of the work will be completed by A in 1 day (since A starts and they work alternately).

⇒ Total time = 4 + 1 = 5 days.

**Therefore, the work will be completed in 5 days.**

questions.question: If a diamond ring is sold for Rs. 5,94,320, then a woman will get a loss of 5%. At what price should she sell it so that her profit becomes 25%?
questions.solution:

Profit should be 25%.

**Concept:**

Calculation of Cost Price and Selling Price.

**Solution:**

⇒ Cost Price = Rs. 5,94,320 / (95/100) = Rs. 6,25,600.

⇒ Selling Price for a profit of 25% = Rs. 6,25,600 × (125/100) = Rs. 7,82,000.

**Therefore, she should sell the diamond ring for Rs. 7,82,000 for a profit of 25%.**

questions.question: In a panchayat election, there were two candidates A and B. Candidate A got 42% of the votes and lost to B by 8000 votes. What is the total number of votes?
questions.solution:
**Given data:**

Candidate A's vote share = 42%

Difference in votes between candidates A and B = 8000 votes

**Concept:**

The difference between the votes of the two candidates can be expressed as a percentage of the total votes.

**Solution:**

Candidate B's vote share = 100% - 42% = 58%

The difference between the vote shares of B and A = 58% - 42% = 16%

⇒ 16% of Total votes = 8000 votes

We can find the total number of votes (T) from this equation

⇒ T = 8000 / (16 / 100)

⇒ T = 8000 × 100 / 16

⇒ T = 50000

**Therefore the total number of votes is 50000.**
